title: Pushing a finite type ideal along an etale ring map into a product involving an ideal of the base
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For an etale ring map A -> B, a nonzerodivisor a in A facing a finite type ideal J of B whose vanishing locus sits inside V(aB), the lemma asserts that for every prime q of B there is a finite type ideal I of A with V(I) inside V(a) and an element g not in q such that IB_g = JJ' for some finite type ideal J' of B_g (statement lines 8875-8883). The proof localises at g to make B standard etale, hence a localisation C_h of C = A[x]/(f) with f monic of degree d, takes generators h_1, ..., h_n of J over B, uses the condition V(J) inside V(aB) to write a^m as a B-linear combination of the h_i, adds h_{n+1} = a^m, and takes I = Fit_0(C/(h_1, ..., h_{r+1})) as in the preceding fitting ideal trick (proof lines 8886-8897). The conclusion follows because C/(h_1, ..., h_{r+1}) is annihilated by a^m, so a^{dm} lies in I, which gives V(I) inside V(a) (proof lines 8898-8900). Reducing to the standard etale case and reading off the exponent dm from the monic equation are the non-formal steps, so the claim is H2.
